payload.selection_rationale:
Only one proposal (practice) was submitted. I took it as the core and checked each piece against what the build check measured in the tree and against the person's decisions on record.

**Why it fits the real code**
- It extends `ShellReveal.Walk` through the seam that already exists. Walk takes injected parse/pathOf/open/free delegates (ShellReveal.cs:211) and is unit-tested through them. One more delegate lets every attribute × settings cell run on real %TEMP% files without changing this PC's Explorer settings, which no engine stage may change.
- It copies a pattern the code already has. `Failed` + `NoLongerExists` already means "nothing was opened, and the App words the reason". The new reason works the same way, so `RevealKind` keeps its two values.
- It copies an existing fitness rule. .taad/fitness.yaml:599-612 already confines `SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems` and `SHParseDisplayName` to ShellReveal.cs.
- It reads the settings with the call Q-175 named. The build check confirmed on this PC that `SHGetSetSettings` answers unelevated and agrees with the registry.

**Why it is the decision on record**
- It builds Q-175, which a person decided: refuse, add a new RevealReason, name the Explorer option.
- The predicate is now fixed by the person's 0-of-13 measurement at Hidden=2 together with SL-088's 0/8 and 5/5 at Hidden=1.

**Why it is the simplest thing that works**
- One read-only P/Invoke per hidden reveal, one predicate, one reason, one status-line branch.
- No COM automation of Explorer (Q-169 and Q-175 rule it out), no settings cache, no ancestor walk.
- The proposal's `over_engineering_flag` was false, and the components agree with it.

**What I changed, against the record**
- **Which setting to name is decided in Core.** Core now computes `HiddenBy` flags, so the App only maps flags to labels. In the proposal the App would have re-derived this from `View` and `System`.
- **A hook failpoint was added**, following the existing `FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING` precedent. Without it, the Windows-default status text could only be checked by a person who changes Explorer's settings.
- **A wrong claim in the proposal is corrected.** It said only one unmeasured cell predicts a landing. There are three: Hidden+System with both settings on, System-only at Hidden=2, and non-hidden items under hidden ancestors at Hidden=2.
- **The window-case rule allows for how fitness treats PowerShell.** Fitness does not blank `#` comments in .ps1 files, so that rule's patterns are anchored so a comment cannot trigger them.

**Baseline for validate**
- The full suite already fails 3 last-access tests (Q-190, unrelated to reveal).
- Reveal should be judged by the ShellReveal filter, which passes 52/52 today, plus the new tests.

components.name: Visibility gate in ShellReveal.Walk
components.responsibility:
A new step after the resolve-back check (ShellReveal.cs:230-231) and before the open (:233).
1. Read the target's attributes with the existing `File.GetAttributes(\\?\ path)`, moved up from :243-259. The volume-root exemption is unchanged, and if the read throws, Hidden and System are both false, as today.
2. Only if the target is Hidden and not a volume root, call the injected explorer delegate once.
3. Compute HiddenBy:
   - HiddenFiles when Hidden && !ShowsHidden;
   - ProtectedFiles when Hidden && System && !ShowsProtected.
4. If HiddenBy is not None, return Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings with HResult 0 and Hidden, System, HiddenBy and View filled in. `open` is never called.
5. Otherwise open as today and return Exact.
components.key_interactions:
The refusal returns inside the existing try, so the finally block at :237-241 still frees the pidl exactly once.

Precedence, first match wins:
1. NameUnaddressable
2. Parse failure (NoLongerExists / None)
3. ParsedAsAnotherItem
4. HiddenByExplorerSettings (new)
5. Open failure
6. Exact

RevealAsync passes `() => override ?? ReadExplorerView()` as the delegate.

components.name: ExplorerView, ExplorerHides and the settings reader
components.responsibility:
- `readonly record struct ExplorerView(bool ShowsHidden, bool ShowsProtected)`, with a pure `Hides(bool hidden, bool system) -> ExplorerHides`.
- `ExplorerHides` is a [Flags] enum: None = 0, HiddenFiles = 1, ProtectedFiles = 2.
- `FromShellState(uint firstDword)` reads bit 0 (fShowAllObjects) and bit 15 (fShowSuperHidden) and ignores every other bit.
- `ReadExplorerView()` P/Invokes shell32 `SHGetSetSettings` with a zeroed buffer of at least 64 bytes, mask SSF_SHOWALLOBJECTS | SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN (0x00040001) and bSet = false, then decodes the first DWORD. It caches nothing and has no write path.
components.key_interactions: This is the only call site of SHGetSetSettings in src, which fitness rule 1 enforces. It runs on the reveal's background STA thread, once per hidden reveal.

components.name: RevealReason / RevealOutcome additions
components.responsibility:
- `RevealKind` stays {Exact, Failed} (ShellReveal.cs:8-12).
- `RevealReason` (:14-20) gains `HiddenByExplorerSettings`.
- `RevealOutcome` gains:
  - `ExplorerHides HiddenBy`: which Explorer setting or settings hide the item, decided in Core;
  - `ExplorerView? View`: null when it wasn't read, kept for the hook's log so a person-run check can see which view the app read.
components.key_interactions: MainWindow.FormatRevealStatus reads `HiddenBy` only. The window hook's reveal record logs `kind`, `reason`, `hiddenBy` and `view`.

components.name: Hook failpoint for Explorer's view
components.responsibility:
- `ShellReveal.OverrideExplorerView(ExplorerView? view)` replaces the real read for the rest of the process; null clears it.
- The window hook sets it only when FSA_HOOK_MODE is set and FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW='<0|1>|<0|1>' (showsHidden|showsProtected), and logs an 'explorer-view-injected' line.
- The product never reads that variable.
components.key_interactions:
It is reached the same way the hook reaches SynchronousIoCancel.FailListingOf for FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING (SL-082). The new variable goes into the hook's variable lists, the ones touched by 47d7154 and acf169e, and the mode check at StartupHook.cs:197-200 and :278.

Window cases may use an injected view only to assert a refusal, never a landing: Explorer itself still follows the real settings.

components.name: Reveal status line
components.responsibility:
FormatRevealStatus (MainWindow.xaml.cs:856-869):
- **New branch** for HiddenByExplorerSettings, placed before the generic 'Couldn't show' fallthrough. Each HiddenBy flag maps to its Folder Options label ('Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives'; 'Hide protected operating system files'). The sentence also names the leaf and says nothing was opened.
- **Exact** now always gives an empty string, so the line collapses (:832). The old blanket hidden note (case 1) is deleted.
- NoLongerExists and 'Couldn't show…' are unchanged.
components.key_interactions: It only maps flags to text. It does not read View, Hidden or System to decide anything.

components.name: Core unit tests for the gate
components.responsibility:
1. **Theory** over real %TEMP% items (plain, S-only, H-only, H+S; files and folders) × the four ExplorerView cells. It asserts that:
   - Kind, Reason and HiddenBy match the predicate;
   - open is called only for Exact;
   - free is called exactly once on every path;
   - the delegate is called only for Hidden targets.
2. **Real-system-item Fact**: C:\System Volume Information and C:\pagefile.sys, through injected parse/pathOf/open and view (true, false). It must read Hidden|System and refuse without calling open.
3. **Volume root (C:\)**: the delegate is never called and the result stays Exact.
4. **Precedence Facts** on hidden targets: NoLongerExists, ParsedAsAnotherItem and NameUnaddressable still win, and the delegate is not called.
5. **FromShellState decode**: 0x0, 0x1, 0x8000, 0x8001 and 0x5.
6. **Read-only real-call Fact**: ReadExplorerView agrees with HKCU Explorer\Advanced Hidden==1 and ShowSuperHidden==1. Absent values are read as Windows' defaults.

The theory replaces Walk_HiddenAndSystemAttributes_DetectedOnExactItem (ShellRevealTests.cs:222-245).
components.key_interactions: Uses the existing injected-delegate seam plus the new explorer delegate. No test writes Explorer settings; fitness rule 4 enforces that.

components.name: Window reveal cases
components.responsibility:
1. **Re-pin the old note.** Rewrite the pagefile.sys text pins at WindowCases.ps1:2150, 2206 and 4360, and the hs_file.sys kind and text pins at :3781-3782.
2. **Derive expectations from the settings in force.** Each case reads HKCU Explorer\Advanced Hidden and ShowSuperHidden read-only at start and works out each target's expected kind, reason, hiddenBy and text from the same predicate. The registry is read on purpose rather than SHGetSetSettings, so the oracle is independent of the app's decode.
3. **New R-series refusal case**, using the next free R- id (written R-003 below):
   - **Settings-in-force step**: an H+S temp file at the owner's (1,0) expects Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings, the protected-files text, and no new Shell.Application window.
   - **Injected-defaults step**: FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=0|0 with an H-only target and an H+S target that has a 200-character leaf, window at its minimum size. It expects the hidden-files text and the both-settings text, no Explorer window, every list keeping one full row, and a case line saying the view was injected.
4. **The Exact-control step** (H-only selected in a real Explorer window at (1,0)) reuses R-002's Shell.Application reading. It is person-run.
components.key_interactions: Reuses R-002's window reading, the leaf / GetLongPathName matching and Close-CaseWindows. The run is void if the registry values change mid-run. A case that would need the settings changed stops and reports itself owed to a person.

components.name: Settled fitness rules
components.responsibility: Four rules appended under '# settled by SL-091'. They are settled, not twinned, so the literal twinned counts in RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1 do not move. See architecture_rules.
components.key_interactions: Rule 1 is modelled on the shell-call rule at :599-612. Rule 3's .ps1 patterns are line-anchored because fitness blanks only // and /* */ comments (SL-065).

components.name: SL-091 design note
components.key_interactions: This is where the next slice finds the unmeasured cells.

key_decisions.decision: When Explorer's settings hide the item, the reveal is refused: Walk opens nothing and the status line names the setting or settings. This is used instead of the brief's 'parent-only' outcome and the derived C2 and C4 wording ('Explorer opened the parent without selecting the item').

The predicate uses only the item's own attributes, and volume roots are exempt. Explorer hides the item when it is Hidden and hidden files aren't shown, or when it is Hidden+System and protected operating system files are hidden.
Explorer's view is read with SHGetSetSettings: read-only, never cached, and only for Hidden, non-root targets.
key_decisions.rationale:
Q-175 names this call. The build check and two spikes saw it agree with the registry on this PC.
- Reading only for Hidden targets keeps today's non-hidden path free of the new call.
- Not caching avoids building a staleness bug on purpose.

If a person's mid-session toggle run shows stale values, only `ReadExplorerView`'s body changes, to a read-only HKCU read. The delegate contract stays the same.

key_decisions.decision: Core decides everything, including which setting or settings to name, and returns them as HiddenBy flags. The App only maps flags to Folder Options labels.
key_decisions.rationale: In the proposal, the App would have chosen which setting to name from View and System. That would put a second copy of the predicate in a project with no App test project. As flags from Core, every naming cell is covered by xUnit, and the App's text is a fixed mapping. This follows the project's line that the App never decides an outcome kind.

Q-175 asks for one new reason, not a new kind. The NoLongerExists precedent already means 'Failed, nothing opened, a reason the App words'.

The consumers are MainWindow, the hook's reveal record and the in-repo tests.

View is nullable so that 'not read' cannot be mistaken for Hidden=2/SSH=0, which is what `default(ExplorerView)` would decode as.

key_decisions.decision: Delete the blanket Exact+Hidden note. Exact now means Explorer will select the item, so the status line collapses.
key_decisions.rationale: The build check measured that the note appears for every hidden item whatever the settings, including on this PC, where Hidden-only items are selected. C4 asks for a statement only when the settings in force mean the item is hidden. The refusal text now does that job.

key_decisions.decision: If the attribute read throws, the item is treated as not hidden (fail-open), as it is today.
key_decisions.rationale: This keeps SL-088's behaviour on a rare path. The risk is concentrated on the items this slice exists for (pagefile.sys, held open by the system; System Volume Information, which the user can't open). So a material case reads their real attributes through Walk. Switching to fail-closed would need its own evidence.

key_decisions.decision: Add a hook failpoint, FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW → ShellReveal.OverrideExplorerView. It may be used only to assert refusals.
key_decisions.rationale:
The slice exists because of Windows defaults, yet no engine stage may set Hidden=2. Injecting the view through the hook makes the defaults status text and the no-window refusal checkable unattended through the shipped exe. It follows the FailListingOf / FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING precedent and the Q-195 convention that the case says it injected.

A landing can never be asserted under an injected view, because Explorer follows the real settings.

Fitness rule 1 keeps product code from calling the override.

key_decisions.decision: This is not a KnownWorkarounds entry.
key_decisions.rationale:
Explorer not listing hidden items while 'show hidden files' is off is Explorer honouring the user's own setting, not a defect outside the project. The defect was this app's: it reported Exact for an item Explorer would not select. A bug in this project's own code is fixed, not toggled.

An 'off' position would bring back that false success. The user's real control is Explorer's own setting, which the status line names.

key_decisions.decision:
Two choices about enforcement and test expectations:
- 'Read-only, ShellReveal.cs only' and 'tests never change Explorer's settings' are settled fitness rules, not twinned ones.
- Window cases derive their expectations from the HKCU values in force, read-only, instead of pinning (1,0) results.
key_decisions.rationale:
Settled rules leave alone the twinned counts pinned literally across RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1, which no gate runs (SL-053, SL-085).

Deriving expectations from the registry has two benefits:
- it gives an oracle independent of the app's SHELLSTATE decode;
- the same steps become the person's Hidden=2 check with no new tooling.

Pinning (1,0) results would make the pins wrong on any machine at Windows defaults.

proposals.note:
Only proposal. Taken as the core: refusal, predicate, injected delegate, uncached SHGetSetSettings read, removal of the blanket note, settled fitness rule, window cases derived from the settings in force.

Changed at seams:
- HiddenBy flags are computed in Core; the App no longer derives which setting to name from View and System.
- Added a hook failpoint so the defaults text is machine-checkable.
- Corrected the claim that only one unmeasured cell predicts Exact (there are three).
- Added rules forbidding writes to Explorer settings from src and from tests, with .ps1 patterns anchored against fitness matching # comments.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so no pieces from different proposals had to be fitted together. Nothing here has survived a disagreement; the reviewer is the first to argue with it.

What I checked against the record, and what I changed:

1. **Decisions on record.** Q-175 (a person) says refuse and open nothing. Q-169 (a model) and the brief / build-check derived C2 and C4 say open the parent and report parent-only. These cannot both ship. I kept Q-175 and restated how C2-C4 are met. I did not build both.

2. **Who decides.** The proposal had Core decide whether to refuse while the App decided which setting to name, by reading View and System: two owners of one predicate. I moved the naming into Core as HiddenBy flags, so the App only maps flags to labels.

3. **Failpoint vs. landing assertions.** An injected Explorer view and a real Explorer landing contradict each other, because Explorer follows the real settings. So the injected view is allowed only for refusal assertions, and every landing step runs at the real settings and is person-run.

4. **The proposal's safety claim.** It said every unmeasured cell except Hidden+System at (1,1) errs toward refusal. That is false. System-only at Hidden=2 and non-hidden items under hidden ancestors at Hidden=2 also predict Exact without a measurement. Corrected in key_decisions and in the transfer invariants.

5. **Moving the attribute read ahead of the open.** It still sits inside the try, so the finally block frees the pidl once. The volume-root exemption and the fail-open on exceptions are kept. Precedence keeps NoLongerExists ahead of the refusal, so a vanished hidden item still says 'rescan'.

6. **Existing pins.** WindowCases.ps1:2150, 2206 and 4360 (pagefile.sys text) and :3781-3782 (hs_file.sys kind='Exact'), plus ShellRevealTests.cs:222-245 (Kind=Exact for H+S), contradict the new behaviour. All are re-pinned. They are not left beside it.

7. **Fitness and .ps1 comments.** Fitness does not blank # comments in .ps1, so a commented example would trip the window-case rule. Its patterns are anchored to lines with no # before the command.

8. **Workaround list.** The KnownWorkarounds rule was checked and does not apply: the defect was this project's own false success report.

9. **Baselines, not regressions.** The three failing last-access tests (Q-190) are unrelated to reveal.

architecture_rules.name: only ShellReveal.cs reads Explorer's view settings or overrides them
architecture_rules.because:
Breaking this lets two pieces of code decide whether a reveal is refused:
- A second reader elsewhere would give a second, independently decoded answer, and the App's status line would drift from Core's verdict.
- A product call to the hook failpoint would let something other than the shell's own state decide the refusal.

The shell-call rule at .taad/fitness.yaml:599-612 already holds the same line for SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems and SHParseDisplayName.

architecture_rules.name: the app never writes Explorer's settings
architecture_rules.because: The project promises the app never changes anything, and SL-088's go verdict and Q-175 both say it never changes Explorer's settings to make a reveal land. SHGetSetSettings with bSet=TRUE, or a writable open of HKCU Explorer\Advanced, would silently change how the user's Explorer shows every folder.

architecture_rules.name: the window cases never change the person's Explorer settings
architecture_rules.because: These cases now read Hidden and ShowSuperHidden to derive their expectations, and the build and validate stages run them unattended. Changing Explorer's settings is a machine-setting change only the person may make (build check; all three risk spikes stopped for it). A case that flips Hidden to 2 to 'test the defaults' would change the owner's desktop without asking. Patterns are line-anchored because fitness does not blank # comments in .ps1.

architecture_rules.name: the Core tests never change the person's Explorer settings
architecture_rules.because: ShellRevealTests gains a real-call Fact that reads HKCU Explorer\Advanced and SHGetSetSettings. A test that set the values to cover the other cells would change the owner's Explorer on every unattended `dotnet test`. The other cells are covered by the injected delegate instead.

cases.shape: the item is not Hidden: a plain file or folder, or a System-only one
cases.why:
Walk branches on Hidden alone.
- A non-hidden item must skip the settings read and keep today's Exact path.
- System-only items are predicted visible (measured selected 8/8 at the owner's 1/0), so a predicate that refuses on System alone would refuse reveals that land.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests visibility theory, rows plain and S-only (file and folder) × all four ExplorerView cells. Expects Kind=Exact, open called once, explorer delegate never called.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: a Hidden-only item while Explorer shows hidden files (the owner's PC: ShowsHidden=true, ShowsProtected=false)
cases.why: This is the C5 regression guard. Hidden-only items land 5/5 here. A gate that refuses on Hidden alone would break the owner's everyday reveals of AppData-style items, and the status line must now be empty.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests visibility theory, rows H-only file and folder at view (true, false). Expects Exact, HiddenBy=None, open called once, free called once.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: a Hidden-only item while Explorer hides hidden files (Windows default: ShowsHidden=false)
cases.why: The measured 0/13: the parent opens with nothing selected and S_OK is returned, so today's code reports Exact. This is C2.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests visibility theory, rows H-only at views (false, false) and (false, true). Expects Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings, HiddenBy=HiddenFiles, HResult 0, open never called, free called exactly once.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: a Hidden+System item while hidden files are shown but protected files are hidden (the owner's PC)
cases.why: This is the false success affecting the owner today: SL-088 selected 0 of 8 here and still reported Exact. It is C3. The status line must name only the protected-files setting, because hidden files are already shown.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests visibility theory, rows H+S file and folder at view (true, false). Expects Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings, HiddenBy=ProtectedFiles only, open never called, free called once.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: a Hidden+System item with both settings hiding it (Windows default)
cases.why: Both flags must be reported. Naming one would send the user to flip one box and still find nothing selected.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests visibility theory, rows H+S at view (false, false). Expects HiddenBy=HiddenFiles|ProtectedFiles, open never called.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: a Hidden+System item with hidden files and protected files both shown
cases.why: This is the only H+S cell the predicate lets through, and it is unmeasured (spike cell 1 not run). Pinning it means a person's cell-1 result changes exactly one row instead of hiding in a formula.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests visibility theory, rows H+S at view (true, true). Expects Exact, open called once.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: the item is one Windows protects: C:\System Volume Information (a folder the user cannot open) and C:\pagefile.sys (held open by the system, error 32 on any open)
cases.why: The attribute read moves ahead of the open. If it throws on these items, they count as not hidden and the false landing returns for exactly the items this slice exists for. Temp plants cannot reproduce either refusal: NTFS grants read-attributes through the parent's list right (U-107), and no user process can hold a file the way the paging file is held.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests real-system-item Fact, read-only. It uses the real paths with injected parse/pathOf/open and view (true, false), opens no window, and expects Hidden=System=true, HiddenBy=ProtectedFiles, open never called.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: the target is a volume root (C:\), whose directory carries Hidden|System
cases.why: The root exemption must hold in the new gate. Otherwise every drive-root reveal is refused at Windows defaults.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests volume-root Fact with view (false, false). Expects Exact and the explorer delegate never called.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: a Hidden+System target that fails earlier: it no longer exists, it parses as another item, or its name is unaddressable
cases.why: Precedence: the refusal must not mask 'no longer exists, rescan' or the name diagnostics, and the pidl must still be freed once.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests precedence Facts on hidden targets with view (false, false). Expect NoLongerExists / ParsedAsAnotherItem / NameUnaddressable unchanged, delegate never called, free called once where a pidl exists.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: the first SHELLSTATE DWORD is 0x0, 0x1, 0x8000, 0x8001, or 0x5 (an unrelated bit set, as the build check saw)
cases.why: Bit 15 (fShowSuperHidden) has never been seen at 1 on this PC, and other bits must be ignored. A mis-decode silently changes which H+S items are refused.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests FromShellState Facts: (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), and 0x5 → (1,0).
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.shape: the real SHGetSetSettings call on this PC
cases.why: Proves the P/Invoke buffer, mask and decode against the live shell, with the registry as an independent oracle.
cases.check:
ShellRevealTests real-call Fact, read-only. ReadExplorerView().ShowsHidden == (HKCU Explorer\Advanced Hidden == 1) and ShowsProtected == (ShowSuperHidden == 1); absent values are read as 2 and 0.
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal"

cases.behaviour: show a refused reveal on the status line
cases.shape: the settings actually in force on this PC (Hidden=1, ShowSuperHidden=0), with a Hidden+System temp file revealed through the shipped exe
cases.why: Checks the real settings read end to end. The old pins (WindowCases.ps1:2150, 2206, 4360, 3781-3782) expect Exact and the old note, and the refusal must open no Explorer window.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-003 (new refusal case, next free R- id; settings-in-force step). Expects a hook record of Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings / hiddenBy=ProtectedFiles, the protected-files text, and no new Shell.Application window.

cases.behaviour: show a refused reveal on the status line
cases.shape: Explorer's view injected as Windows defaults (FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=0|0), with a Hidden-only target and a Hidden+System target with a 200-character leaf, window at its minimum size
cases.why: This is the only unattended way to see the defaults texts (hidden-files only, and both settings) through the shipped exe. The longest new text must not take a list's last full row (Q-049's rule).

cases.shape: the attribute read throws (the item is removed between the resolve-back and the read)
cases.why: It is a race only. Fail-open keeps SL-088's behaviour unchanged, and the next reveal reports NoLongerExists. Testing it would need a new race seam in Walk for a path no real input reaches deliberately.

contracts.name: ShellReveal.Walk(plan, requested, parse, pathOf, open, free, explorer)
contracts.notes:
New parameter: `Func<ExplorerView> explorer`.
- It is called at most once, only after the resolve-back succeeds, and only for a Hidden target that is not a volume root.
- When `view.Hides(hidden, system)` is not None, Walk returns Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings with HResult 0 and Hidden, System, HiddenBy and View set. `open` is never called.
- All other outcomes are unchanged.
contracts.error_cases:
- Attribute read throws: Hidden = System = false, and the Exact path is taken (unchanged).
- NameUnaddressable, parse failure (NoLongerExists / None) and ParsedAsAnotherItem keep precedence, and the delegate is not called.
- Open fails after a visible verdict: Failed / None with that hr (unchanged).
- On every path the pidl is freed exactly once.
contracts.auth_model: Ordinary user, no elevation. Reads attributes and shell state only.

contracts.name: ExplorerView, ExplorerHides, ReadExplorerView(), FromShellState(uint)
contracts.notes:
- `ExplorerView(bool ShowsHidden, bool ShowsProtected)`.
- `Hides(hidden, system)` = (hidden && !ShowsHidden ? HiddenFiles : 0) | (hidden && system && !ShowsProtected ? ProtectedFiles : 0).
- `ReadExplorerView` calls `SHGetSetSettings(zeroed buffer ≥ 64 bytes, 0x00040001, bSet: false)`. ShowsHidden is bit 0 and ShowsProtected is bit 15 of the first DWORD; other bits are ignored.
- It is read fresh at each hidden reveal and never written. Fitness rules 1 and 2 enforce the call site and the read-only call.
contracts.error_cases: The API returns void, so there is no failure value. If bit 15 is mis-decoded as always 0, H+S items are refused even when the user shows protected files: lost reach, not a false report.

contracts.name: RevealOutcome additions
contracts.notes:
- `RevealReason.HiddenByExplorerSettings`.
- `ExplorerHides HiddenBy` ([Flags]: None = 0, HiddenFiles = 1, ProtectedFiles = 2).
- `ExplorerView? View`: null when it wasn't read.
- RevealKind stays {Exact, Failed}.

Consumers: MainWindow.FormatRevealStatus (HiddenBy only), the hook's reveal record (kind, reason, hiddenBy, view), and ShellRevealTests.

contracts.name: Reveal status line text
contracts.notes:
- **Exact**: empty, so the line collapses. The old "'<leaf>' is hidden, so Explorer only highlights it if…" note is removed.
- **HiddenByExplorerSettings** must name each flagged Folder Options setting, name the leaf, and say nothing was opened. Defaults:
  - HiddenFiles: "Explorer is set to 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives', which hides '<leaf>', so nothing was opened."
  - ProtectedFiles: "Explorer is set to 'Hide protected operating system files', which hides '<leaf>', so nothing was opened."
  - Both: "Explorer is set to 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives' and 'Hide protected operating system files', which hide '<leaf>', so nothing was opened."
- NoLongerExists and 'Couldn't show…' are unchanged.

The labels are recalled; the builder checks them on Windows 11 26200.
contracts.error_cases: With a long leaf, the both-settings text must still leave every list one full row at 560x644. Case R-003's injected step checks this.

contracts.name: FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW hook failpoint
contracts.notes: FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW='<0|1>|<0|1>' (showsHidden|showsProtected). It requires FSA_HOOK_MODE, like FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING. The hook calls ShellReveal.OverrideExplorerView once at start and logs 'explorer-view-injected' with the values. The product never reads the variable.
contracts.error_cases:
- A malformed value: the hook refuses to start the case and says why.
- An injected view may be used only to assert a refusal. A case that would expect Exact under an injected view is a test defect, because Explorer follows the real settings.

contracts.name: Window-case reveal expectations
contracts.notes:
- WindowCases.ps1 reads HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced Hidden and ShowSuperHidden read-only at start, treating absent values as 2 and 0.
- It derives each target's expected kind, reason, hiddenBy and text from the same predicate.
- A refusal step asserts that no new Shell.Application window appears.
- An Exact step asserts the parent window and the selected leaf, as R-002 does, and is person-run.
contracts.error_cases:
- If the registry values change mid-run, the run is void and the case says so.
- A step that needs other settings stops and reports itself owed to a person. It never writes them; fitness rule 3 enforces that.
contracts.auth_model: Never writes Explorer settings. Changing them is the person's to do.

This held for short and >260-character temp items and for real items including C:\System Volume Information. The plain control lands 4/4.

decidable_disagreements.question: At Windows defaults (Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0), does a Hidden or Hidden+System ancestor stop Explorer selecting a non-hidden item inside it? Examples: AppData\Local, ProgramData\Microsoft, files under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp.
decidable_disagreements.positions:
- This design assumes only the item's own attributes matter. It was measured 13/13 at Hidden=1 only.
- The alternative: Walk reads every ancestor's attributes, and the refusal names the hidden ancestor instead of the leaf.

Spike 'hidden-ancestor-does-not-block-selection-at-defaults' has a harness ready. It needs a person to set 'Don't show hidden files' and run it.

prior_art.pattern: A Tauri app replaced the opener plugin's SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems reveal with `explorer /select`, spawned without checking the exit code ('explorer returns non-zero even on success'). That makes the reveal fire-and-forget with no success signal. U-114 measured /select silently misrouting at 300+ characters, so this is the path to avoid.

'Reveal in Explorer' silently opened the parent folder instead of selecting the file, with no error or dialog, because of argument quoting. Nobody noticed until users reported it. It is the same silent-parent symptom this slice stops reporting as success.
reveal_item_in_dir canonicalizes the path and calls the platform reveal, with no check of the target's visibility or the shell's hidden-file settings.

Chromium's Windows ShowItemInFolder: SHParseDisplayName + SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems, falling back to opening the containing folder. There is no hidden-setting check. This is the 'open the parent anyway' behaviour Q-175 chose not to ship.

SHGetSetSettings with SSF_SHOWALLOBJECTS | SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN filling SHELLSTATE.fShowAllObjects / fShowSuperHidden is the documented read of Explorer's hidden-item view state. Registry Advanced\Hidden is the backing store, not the contract.
Before a dispatch that gives no failure signal, ask the dispatcher's own resolution rule whether it will succeed (canOpenURL / resolveActivity).

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Mobile intent and URL dispatch (iOS canOpenURL, Android resolveActivity)
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The product may not confirm the landing after the fact (Q-169 and Q-175 ban COM automation of Explorer). When a call reports success either way, a preflight against the target's own rule is the only honest option left. The analogy also brings over the right worry, query/dispatch drift, which is why most invariants are must-verify.

invariants.precondition: Explorer's hidden-item filter is the global setting SHGetSetSettings reports, not a per-folder view state.
invariants.evidence:
Every measured cell matches:
- at (1,0): Hidden-only 5/5 selected, H+S 0/8; plain and System-only 8/8; the harness check over 21 targets selected plain, H and S but not H+S;
- at (2,0): H and H+S 0/13, control 4/4.
SHGetSetSettings agreed with the registry on this PC.

invariants.precondition: The query is fresh in a long-running WPF process after the person changes the setting in Explorer.
invariants.evidence: Spike 'shgetsetsettings-tracks-midsession-toggle': harness proven at baseline only.

invariants.precondition: Bit 15 of SHELLSTATE's first DWORD is fShowSuperHidden and reads 1 when protected files are shown.
invariants.evidence: Only ever seen as 0 (ShowSuperHidden=0 on this PC).

invariants.precondition: Where an unmeasured cell predicts refusal, a wrong prediction costs reach, not honesty.
